[Poster for SPIDER BABY SPIDER BABY (1967, USA, Jack Hill) A decrepit mansion houses the Merrye family, whose surviving children suffer from a bizarre, degenerative disease that makes them increasingly violent, cunning, and feral. As outsiders arrive, the family’s twisted games and macabre antics escalate, revealing their darkly comic, horrifying nature and the strange, grotesque world they inhabit. Spider Baby blends black comedy, gothic horror, and campy thrills into a deliriously twisted fable. With its eccentric characters, claustrophobic setting, and outrageous yet eerie atmosphere, the film has become a cult classic of macabre American cinema. Runtime: 79 mins Certificate: 18 Wednesday 28/10 Bar 6pm Film 6:30pm Digital Book here](https://thenickel.co.uk/screening/728)

[Poster for BABY BLOOD BABY BLOOD (1990, France, Alain Robak) A parasitic creature escapes from the body of an exotic animal and takes refuge inside Yanka, a performer in a travelling circus. Now carrying an unnatural pregnancy, she hears the creature speaking to her and is compelled to satisfy its endless demand for human blood. As Yanka cuts a violent path across France, the relationship between mother and unborn monster becomes increasingly intimate and difficult to escape. Alain Robak’s splattery French body-horror comedy combines the biological nightmare of early Cronenberg with the unruly energy of European exploitation cinema. Emmanuelle Escourrou gives a fearless physical performance, shifting between terror, fury and reluctant maternal attachment as the carnage mounts. Grotesque, funny and unexpectedly sympathetic towards its heroine, BABY BLOOD has grown into a fiercely loved cult discovery. Runtime: 88 mins Certificate: 18 Wednesday 28/10 Bar 8:10pm Film 8:40pm Digital Book here](https://thenickel.co.uk/screening/765)

![Poster for ERASERHEAD (ON 16MM)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/uvjn3s5UpPaXOgAAXf8iuMztM2W.jpg)

ERASERHEAD (ON 16MM)

(1977, USA, David Lynch)

Henry Spencer has a room, a girlfriend and a newborn baby. None of them offers much comfort. Outside, machinery groans; inside, the infant cries and a woman in the radiator promises that everything will be fine.

David Lynch’s handmade first feature turns the terrors of parenthood, sex and responsibility into an entirely private industrial universe. Stark monochrome images and Alan Splet’s enveloping sound make the nightmare physical. Horrifying, oddly tender and very funny in places you may not expect, ERASERHEAD remains an experience that resists explanation and rewards surrender.

Introduced by Dominic Hicks and presented on 16mm with a reel intermission and programme notes.

MS. 45 PLUS ✝✝✝ BASEMENT NUNSPLOITATION COSTUME PARTY ✝✝✝

(1981, USA, Abel Ferrara)

A timid, mute seamstress is attacked and raped twice in one day. Traumatized by the assaults, she kills her second attacker, takes his handgun, and begins roaming the streets of New York after dark, randomly shooting men with a .45 caliber pistol.

Set against the grime of early 1980s Manhattan, the film gradually shifts from exploitation thriller to a bleak portrait of trauma, alienation, and urban violence. Its uncompromising tone and Zoë Lund's remarkable central performance have made it one of the defining films of the rape-revenge cycle.

Come dressed as a nun or priest and join our basement party till late!

DOWN TERRACE + BEN WHEATLEY Q&A + FREE SIGNED FANZINE

(2009, United Kingdom, Ben Wheatley)

F&TT&N 5 Launch screening! We celebrate the launch of Ben Wheatley's latest fanzine - film & television Thoughts & notes 5 - the Low Budget issue: with a special screening and Q&A with ben of his debut feature DOWN TERRACE - made for less than £10K in 2009 Ben's latest fanzine unpacks some of the thoughts, processes and mistakes in making the film. It also features an interview with Charlotte regan about making her debut feature Scrapper. Every ticket to this event comes with a copy of the fanzine. Be the first to get one - only at The Nickel.

In Down Terrace, father and son Bill and Karl return from prison to their Brighton home convinced that somebody inside their small criminal operation betrayed them. As suspicion closes around the family kitchen, domestic sniping, old resentments and sudden violence make every cup of tea feel like an interrogation.

Ben Wheatley’s debut turns the British gangster film inside out, replacing swagger with cramped rooms, black comedy and the queasy intimacy of a family destroying itself. Shot with collaborators who would become central to his career, it is a remarkably assured statement of the mordant humour and eruptive menace to come.

Ben Wheatley joins us on stage to discuss the film, and all ticketholders will receive a highly limited edition autographed fanzine.

[Poster for GODS OF TIMES SQUARE GODS OF TIMES SQUARE (1999, USA, Richard Sandler) Before the corporate billboards swallowed the skyline, Times Square had other voices: street preachers, prophets, conspiracy theorists and people who believed the end was close. ANOTHER WOMAN (16MM)

Opened in June 2025, The Nickel Cinema is a truly independent repertory theatre dedicated to underseen cinema.

The venue contains a 37-seater cinema space equipped with a 133" screen, Sony VPL-XW5000 4K laser projector, 16mm film projector, stage mic, dynamic lighting and supports Prores/MP4, Bluray, DVD and VHS formats.

The spacious basement bar is ideal for parties, discussions and events. We stock beer, wine, spirits, cocktails and freshly cooked popcorn.
